from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Meet Pip, the squirrel who loves organizing his acorns.",
            "Three acorns offer six ways to arrange them.",
            "Two acorns have two ways; one has one.",
            "How many ways can Pip arrange zero acorns?",
            "Most guess zero, but the answer is one!"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Squirrel's Dilemma", lines)

        # Colors
        PIP_COLOR = "#D2B48C"
        ACORN_COLOR = "#CD853F"
        TEXT_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # Simple Pip Squirrel Representation
        pip_body = Circle(radius=0.5, color=PIP_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        pip_head = Circle(radius=0.3, color=PIP_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.4)
        pip_ear_l = Triangle(color=PIP_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).move_to(pip_head.get_top() + LEFT*0.1)
        pip_ear_r = Triangle(color=PIP_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).move_to(pip_head.get_top() + RIGHT*0.1)
        pip = VGroup(pip_body, pip_head, pip_ear_l, pip_ear_r)

        # Shelf
        shelf = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GREY).scale(2)

        # Acorns
        def create_acorn():
            body = Ellipse(width=0.4, height=0.5, color=ACORN_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
            cap = Arc(radius=0.2, angle=PI, color="#8B4513", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.2)
            return VGroup(body, cap).scale(0.6)

        acorns = VGroup(create_acorn(), create_acorn(), create_acorn())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(pip, "B1", "E2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(shelf, "D3", "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(pip), Create(shelf))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Position acorns on shelf
        for i, acorn in enumerate(acorns):
            self.place_at_grid(acorn, f"C{i+4}")
        
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency errors
        label_3factorial = Text("3! = 6", color=TEXT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(label_3factorial, "B5")

        self.play(FadeIn(acorns))
        self.play(Write(label_3factorial))

        # Permutation visualization (quick cycling)
        positions = [acorns[0].get_center(), acorns[1].get_center(), acorns[2].get_center()]
        perms = [[0, 2, 1], [1, 0, 2], [1, 2, 0], [2, 0, 1], [2, 1, 0]]
        
        for p in perms:
            self.play(
                acorns[0].animate.move_to(positions[p[0]]),
                acorns[1].animate.move_to(positions[p[1]]),
                acorns[2].animate.move_to(positions[p[2]]),
                run_time=0.3
            )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        label_2factorial = Text("2! = 2", color=TEXT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(label_2factorial, "B5")
        
        label_1factorial = Text("1! = 1", color=TEXT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(label_1factorial, "B5")

        # Show 2 acorns
        self.play(FadeOut(acorns[2]), FadeOut(label_3factorial))
        self.play(Write(label_2factorial))
        self.play(acorns[0].animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]), acorns[1].animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(acorns[0].animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]), acorns[1].animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Show 1 acorn
        self.play(FadeOut(acorns[1]), FadeOut(label_2factorial))
        self.play(Write(label_1factorial))
        self.play(acorns[0].animate.move_to(self.grid["C4.5"] if "C4.5" in self.grid else self.grid["C4"]), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        thought_bubble = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(thought_bubble, "B3")
        thought_text = Text("0! = ?", color=TEXT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(thought_text, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeOut(acorns[0]), FadeOut(label_1factorial))
        self.play(Create(thought_bubble), Write(thought_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        giant_one = Text("1", font_size=120, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(giant_one, "C4", "E5")

        self.play(FadeIn(giant_one, shift=UP))
        self.play(Indicate(giant_one))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A factorial, written as n!, is a special product.",
            "It multiplies positive integers from n down to one.",
            "Factorials count the ways to arrange unique objects.",
            "Three objects mean three times two times one.",
            "This multiplication results in six possible arrangements."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: What is a Factorial?", lecture_lines)
        
        # Helper to create a bird
        def create_bird(color):
            body = Triangle(color=color, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.2)
            eye = Dot(color=BLACK).scale(0.3).move_to(body.get_top() + DOWN*0.05)
            return VGroup(body, eye)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to bypass FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        formula = Text("n! = n × (n - 1) × ... × 1", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.play(FadeOut(rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        meaning_text = Text("n! = ways to arrange n items", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(meaning_text, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(meaning_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # Wire and Birds
        wire = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D6"], color=GRAY)
        bird_red = create_bird("#FF0000")
        bird_blue = create_bird("#0000FF")
        bird_green = create_bird("#00FF00")
        
        # Position birds on wire with safe grid access
        bird_red.move_to(self.grid["D2"])
        bird_blue.move_to(self.grid["D3.5"] if "D3.5" in self.grid else (self.grid["D3"] + self.grid["D4"])/2)
        bird_green.move_to(self.grid["D5"])

        self.play(Create(wire))
        self.play(FadeIn(bird_red, bird_blue, bird_green, shift=UP))
        
        calc_3 = Text("3 × 2 × 1 = 6", font_size=32).next_to(wire, UP)
        self.play(Write(calc_3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Swap 1
        self.play(
            bird_red.animate.move_to(bird_blue.get_center()),
            bird_blue.animate.move_to(bird_red.get_center()),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        # Swap 2
        self.play(
            bird_blue.animate.move_to(bird_green.get_center()),
            bird_green.animate.move_to(bird_blue.get_center()),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Extra Visuals: Fade out one bird, show calculation changes
        self.play(FadeOut(bird_green), FadeOut(calc_3))
        calc_2 = Text("2 × 1 = 2", font_size=32).next_to(wire, UP)
        self.play(Write(calc_2))
        self.play(
            bird_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"]),
            bird_blue.animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            bird_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]),
            bird_blue.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"]),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        self.play(FadeOut(bird_blue), FadeOut(calc_2))
        calc_1 = Text("1 = 1", font_size=32).next_to(wire, UP)
        self.play(Write(calc_1))
        self.play(bird_red.animate.move_to((self.grid["D1"] + self.grid["D6"])/2))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            "We can find factorials by dividing the next one.",
            "Divide three! by three to get two!",
            "Divide two! by two to get one!",
            "Finally, divide one! by one to find zero!",
            "This logical pattern reveals that zero! must be one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Pattern: Working Backwards", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        formula = Text("(n-1)! = n! / n", color="#00FFFF", font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        fact_3 = Text("3! = 6", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(fact_3, "B3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        fact_2 = Text("2! = 2", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(fact_2, "C3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        arrow_1 = Arrow(start=self.grid["B4"], end=self.grid["C4"], color="#FFFFFF", buff=0.1)
        # Using unicode division symbol instead of LaTeX \div
        label_1 = Text("÷ 3", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=28)
        label_1.next_to(arrow_1, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(fact_3))
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_1), Write(label_1))
        self.play(Write(fact_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        fact_1 = Text("1! = 1", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(fact_1, "D3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        arrow_2 = Arrow(start=self.grid["C4"], end=self.grid["D4"], color="#FFFFFF", buff=0.1)
        label_2 = Text("÷ 2", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=28)
        label_2.next_to(arrow_2, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_2), Write(label_2))
        self.play(Write(fact_1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        fact_0 = Text("0! = 1", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(fact_0, "E3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        arrow_3 = Arrow(start=self.grid["D4"], end=self.grid["E4"], color="#FFFFFF", buff=0.1)
        label_3 = Text("÷ 1", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=28)
        label_3.next_to(arrow_3, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_3), Write(label_3))
        self.play(Write(fact_0))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        gold_box = SurroundingRectangle(fact_0, color="#FFD700", buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(gold_box))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(Scene):

        # 1. Setup Layout Components
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        
        # Title
        title_text = "The Mystery of 0: Why Nothing is Something"
        title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # Lecture Notes (Left Side)
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Placeholders in Numerals",
            "- The Concept of Void",
            "- Zero as an Identity Element",
            "- Limits and Infinitesimals"
        ]
        
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) 
            for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        lecture_vgroup.to_edge(LEFT, buff=1.0)
        
        # 2. Define Visual Grid (Right Side)
        # Using a dictionary for coordinate mapping (3x3 grid for the right half)
        grid_positions = {
            "A1": [2, 2, 0], "A2": [4, 2, 0], "A3": [6, 2, 0],
            "B1": [2, 0, 0], "B2": [4, 0, 0], "B3": [6, 0, 0],
            "C1": [2, -2, 0], "C2": [4, -2, 0], "C3": [6, -2, 0],
        }

        # 3. Create Visual Objects
        # Zero Concept Representation
        circle_zero = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE).move_to(grid_positions["B2"])
        # Replacing Tex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex' dependency
        empty_set = Text("∅", font_size=72, color=YELLOW).move_to(grid_positions["A2"])
        number_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-2, 2, 1], length=3, include_numbers=True, label_constructor=Text).move_to(grid_positions["C2"])
        
        # 4. Animation Sequence
        # Intro Title and Lecture
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        for line in lecture_vgroup:
            self.play(FadeIn(line, shift=RIGHT * 0.2), run_time=0.6)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # Visualizations on the right
        # Show Empty Set
        self.play(Create(empty_set))
        self.play(empty_set.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(GOLD), run_time=1)
        
        # Transition to Zero Circle
        self.play(Transform(empty_set.copy(), circle_zero))
        self.play(Indicate(circle_zero, color=WHITE))
        
        # Show Number Line context
        self.play(Create(number_line))
        
        # Highlight Zero on Number Line
        zero_dot = Dot(number_line.n2p(0), color=RED, radius=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(zero_dot, scale=2))
        self.play(Flash(zero_dot, color=RED, line_length=0.3))

        # Final hold
        self.wait(3)

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, pos_array):
        """Helper to move mobject to defined grid position."""
        mobject.move_to(pos_array)
        return mobject

outline.topic: The Mystery of 0!: Why Nothing is Something
outline.target_audience: High school students or curious learners with basic algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Hook: The Squirrel's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce a character, 'Pip the Squirrel,' who organizes acorns in a line. We know Pip has 3 ways to arrange 3 acorns (3!), 2 ways for 2 (2!), and 1 way for 1 (1!). But what happens when Pip has 0 acorns? Most people guess 0, but the mathematical answer is 1. This section sets the 'Counter-intuitive' hook for the video.
sections.example: Visual: Pip looking at an empty shelf. A thought bubble shows '0! = ?' with a giant glowing '1' appearing, much to Pip's confusion.

sections.title: Prerequisite: What is a Factorial?
sections.content: Define n! as the product of all positive integers from n down to 1. Explain the physical meaning: the number of ways to arrange 'n' unique objects in a row. Use a simple 3-2-1 countdown visual.
sections.example: Visual: 3 colorful birds (Red, Blue, Green) landing on a wire. Show the 6 possible permutations (3 x 2 x 1 = 6). Then show 2 birds (2 x 1 = 2) and 1 bird (1 way).

sections.title: The Pattern: Working Backwards
sections.content: Introduce the recursive relationship: (n-1)! = n! / n. This is a crucial logical step. If we want to find the previous factorial, we divide the current one by the current number of objects. We will use a 'Step-Down' ladder graphic.
sections.example: Math Visual: 4! = 24. To get 3!, divide 24 by 4 = 6. To get 2!, divide 6 by 3 = 2. To get 1!, divide 2 by 2 = 1. To get 0!, divide 1 by 1 = 1.

sections.title: The Logic of the 'Empty Set'
sections.content: Explain the combinatorial logic. In mathematics, 'arranging nothing' is still an action. There is exactly one way to arrange zero items: by doing absolutely nothing. This is known as the 'Empty Set' arrangement.
sections.example: Visual: A magician's hat. If the hat is empty, how many ways can you arrange the 'nothing' inside? You can't move anything around, so that 'state of emptiness' is the single, unique configuration.

sections.title: The Big Picture: Consistency is King
sections.content: Explain why 0! = 1 is necessary for higher math. Show the formula for 'n choose k' (combinations). If 0! were 0, the formula for choosing all items from a set would involve dividing by zero, which would break mathematics.
sections.example: Visual: A bridge where 0! is the keystone. If 0! = 0, the bridge collapses. If 0! = 1, the formulas for Taylor Series and Binomial Theorems stand strong and stable.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Squirrel's Dilemma
lecture_lines: Meet Pip, a squirrel who loves organizing his acorns.
Three acorns can be arranged in six different ways.
But how many ways can Pip arrange zero acorns?
animations: Fade in Pip the squirrel (color #D2B48C) on the left and a shelf with 3 acorns (color #CD853F) on the right.
Show the 3 acorns cycling through their 6 permutations quickly, with '3! = 6' (color #FFFFFF) appearing above them.
Remove acorns to show an empty shelf. Pip has a thought bubble with '0! =?' (color #FFFFFF) and then a giant '1' (color #FFFF00) appears.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: What is a Factorial?
lecture_lines: A factorial multiplies integers from n down to one.
Three birds on a wire offer six possible arrangements.
Factorials count the ways to arrange any set of items.
animations: Show 3 birds [Asset: bird.svg] (Red #FF0000, Blue #0000FF, Green #00FF00) sitting on a wire, swapping places to show '3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6' arrangements.

Fade out one bird [Asset: bird.svg], show 2 birds [Asset: bird.svg] swapping (2 ways), then fade out another to show 1 bird [Asset: bird.svg] (1 way). Text 'n! = ways to arrange n items' (color #00FFFF).

storyboard.title: The Pattern: Working Backwards
lecture_lines: We can find factorials by dividing the next one.
Dividing three factorial by three gives us two factorial.
Dividing two factorial by two leaves us with one.
Now, divide one factorial by one to find zero.
This logical pattern proves that zero factorial is one.
animations: Write the equation '(n-1)! = \frac{n!}{n}' (color #00FFFF) at the top of the screen.
Create a vertical list starting with '3! = 6'. An arrow points down to '2!' with label 'divide by 3' (color #FFFFFF).
Next entry: '2! = 2'. An arrow points down to '1!' with label 'divide by 2' (color #FFFFFF).
Next entry: '1! = 1'. An arrow points down to '0!' with label 'divide by 1' (color #FFFFFF).
Final entry: '0! = 1'. Circle the result in a bright gold box (color #FFD700).

storyboard.title: The Logic of the 'Empty Set'
lecture_lines: Imagine an empty magician's hat with nothing inside.
This represents an empty set in mathematics.
There is exactly one way to arrange nothing.
animations: Display a magician's hat (color #4B0082) in the center. Text 'The Set of Nothing' (color #FFFFFF) appears above.
Zoom into the empty hat. A label 'Empty Set' (color #A9A9A9) appears inside.
Text '1 Configuration: Doing Nothing' (color #00FF00) appears below the hat, emphasizing that the absence of action is a unique state.

storyboard.title: The Big Picture: Consistency is King
lecture_lines: The combinations formula helps us choose items from sets.
Let's try choosing all items from a group.
If zero factorial was zero, we'd divide by zero.
Setting it to one keeps our formulas working perfectly.
This definition ensures all of mathematics remains stable.
animations: Show the formula 'n \text{ choose } k = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}' (color #FFFFFF) in the center.
Substitute k=n to show 'n \text{ choose } n = \frac{n!}{n!0!}' (color #FFFFFF).
Flash the '0!' in the denominator with a red warning color (#FF0000) to indicate potential division by zero.
Replace '0!' with '1' (color #00FF00) and show the formula simplifies to '1', representing one way to choose all items.
Visual of a stone bridge [Asset: bridge.svg] (color #808080) where the central keystone is labeled '0! = 1' (color #FFFF00), supporting the structure.
